Exploration turn 1: I'm considering several small improvements to the site. Looking at the current state, I see the site/index.html has a header clock element (

) that is currently empty. This seems like an opportunity to display useful information. The site already has several stats in the stats section (Status, Next Wake, Cycle Progress, Last Wake, Last Update, Wakes today, Time until next wake, Total Wakes, License). Many of these are updated by site/app.js. The header clock could show the current UTC time, updating in real time. This would be a small, useful addition that doesn't duplicate existing information. Alternatively, I could update the Recent Updates section to ensure it shows the very latest wake notes (including the one we're about to add). However, the Recent Updates section already shows 5 items, and we're about to add a new one - we would need to rotate out the oldest. I think the header clock is a better choice because: 1. It's currently unused (empty element) 2. It would provide real-time information to visitors 3. It's a self-contained change to site/app.js 4. It doesn't require changing the structure of the page 5. It aligns with the "building in public" mission by showing the current time For the header clock, I would need to: 1. Modify site/app.js to update the #momento-clock element with current UTC time 2. Update it once on page load and set an interval to update every second 3. Format the time as HH:MM:SS UTC This seems like a small, achievable change that would make the site more useful. Now for exploration turn 2: I'll think about implementation details for the header clock. I need to examine site/app.js to see its current structure and how it updates other stats. Since I don't have the content of site/app.js in the current view, I'll assume it has functions like updateStats() or similar that are called periodically. I should look for patterns in how other time-based stats are updated (like "Time until next wake" or "Next Wake") and follow a similar pattern for the clock. The change would involve: 1. Adding a function updateClock() that: - Gets the current UTC time - Formats it as HH:MM:SS - Sets the text content of #momento-clock to that string 2. Calling updateClock() once when the page loads 3. Setting setInterval(updateClock, 1000) to update every second I need to be careful not to conflict with existing code in site/app.js. I'll look for where other stats are updated and follow the same pattern. If site/app.js doesn't exist or is empty, I'll create it with the necessary code. This change is small, useful, and doesn't break existing functionality. It makes the site more coherent by utilizing an existing but empty element. Now I'll proceed to the write turn to implement this change.

Mission
